newsitem.title: PERU: Peru seeks jail for military torture suspects.
newsitem.headline: Peru seeks jail for military torture suspects.

text.p: A Peruvian military prosecutor has recommended jail sentences of between two and four years for four army officers accused of torturing an intelligence agent, local media reported on Sunday.
Prosecutor Reynaldo Shols also said the officers should each pay damages of $3,800 to the state. In addition three of them should each pay $1,900 each to tortured agent Leonor La Rosa.

La Rosa's fingers and ankles were burnt with a welding gun during a torture session in March that ended when she suffered a vaginal haemorrhage, said Shols' report, which was published in local newspapers.
La Rosa had been under "preventitive arrest" by the military for allegedly leaking intelligence secrets to the press.

The scandal over La Rosa's torture -- and the still unsolved murder of another woman intelligence agent found mutilated on Easter Sunday -- threatens to damage the reputation of Peru's armed forces. They are currently basking in the glory of their successful crushing of a four-month hostage siege by Marxist Tupac Amaru rebels.

Shols recommended four years' imprisonment for Col. Jose Salinas, Maj. Percy Salcedo and Maj. Ricardo Anderson, and two years for Col. Carlos Sanchez. All face charges of disobedience, negligence and abuse of authority in a military tribunal due to give its verdict in coming weeks.
La Rosa's lawyer, Heriberto Benitez, said the sentences recommended were "benign if you take into account that in the civil judiciary the crime of kidnapping is punished with a life sentence."

La Rosa herself faces charges of insubordination and breach of secrecy in granting a television interview from her hospital room in which she said she had learned of a campaign by rogue army officers to intimidate opponents of President Alberto Fujimori. Fujimori has denied such a plan.
